text:
maria: heads-up, getting spikes of apiserver 503s in eu-west1 for the last 8m, ctlmgr queue lagging, etcd leader flipped twice
ajay: seen it, provisioner shows burst of attach failures to gpu-pool-3, conntrack errors in node logs
maria: logs: `level=error msg=attach failed: dial tcp: i/o timeout; conntrack: conntrack: conntrack: No space left on device`
jamie: that looks like natconntrack exhaustion on the egress NAT nodes causing TCP resets to our GPU attach API
lee: metrics: conntrack_count ~ 65534 on nat-eu-west1-1 for the period, dropped packets spike aligns with apiserver 5xxs
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20260321-045 (apiserver 503s eu-west1). Pager duty: ops-oncall
ops-oncall: I'm on it, scaling NAT pool and rotating iptables conntrack timeout to shorter windows as mitigation
ajay: also seeing etcd leader election latency climb to ~1.8s during the same window, follower commits lagged
maria: controller-manager backlog: pods waiting for GPU attach ~120, backlog increase started at 04:12 UTC
jamie: temporary mitigation: adding additional NAT gateway instances reduced conntrack pressure by spreading flows, but underlying issue is churn from k8s API retries + model onboards
lee: quick check: `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide` shows many kube-proxy restarts on nodes with high conntrack usage
maria: what's the customer impact? A handful of infra jobs and model onboarding times are failing, internal SLO for gpu attach 99.9% breached for 6m
tim-product: flagging to product — some customers will see increased onboarding latency, estimate impact window 10-30m depending on fix
ops-oncall: change applied: conntrack max increased and conntrack-ttl lowered, NAT pool + new nodes registered, monitoring baseline restored at 04:22 UTC
ajay: follow-up: we should reduce aggressive exponential retry on attach path to avoid thundering herd when NAT is constrained
jamie: agree. Also we should adjust provisioner to prefer smaller batch size for gpu attaches when net egress > threshold
lee: cost note: adding NAT instances has a bill impact — ~0.6k USD per hour in eu-west1 while active, will revert after stabilization
maria: after fixes, etcd leader election latency back to 200ms, apiserver 5xxs dropped, controller-manager queue drained gradually, no further flaps
ops-oncall: recording runbook run: NAT rotate + conntrack tune worked; filing follow-up ticket for better circuit breakers on attach path (SRE-423)
ajay: adding small code snippet we can try for backoff tuning:
```
// exponential backoff with jitter
retry := func() {
  for i := 0; i < maxRetries; i++ {
    if attach() == nil { return }
    sleep := rand.Int63n((1<<i) * baseMs)
    time.Sleep(time.Duration(sleep) * time.Millisecond)
  }
}
```
maria: action items: 1) revert extra NAT infra after 20m stable 2) implement attach backoff change + canary 3) dashboard alert for conntrack > 60k -> escalate
tim-product: I'll notify a couple customers and prepare a short postmortem blurb if needed
jamie: I'll open the PR for provisioner batching change and add a flag for net-sensitive mode
lee: created cost-offset ticket to analyze reserved NAT vs burst autoscale
sre-bot: INC-20260321-045 marked resolved at 04:32 UTC (status: mitigated)
ops-oncall: will monitor for 45m and then start teardown of temporary NAT nodes if stable
maria: thanks all — good catch on conntrack being the choke point, let's keep the follow-ups concise in SRE-423
